clue.text: Capital Radio's set down area

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard rather than seen, so what follows is judged by its sound

parts.note: to anchor a ship is to set it down at its mooring; A is a standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A London radio station has a designated drop-off zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital Radio' reads as the London station, but 'Capital' is the definition and 'Radio's' signals a sound-alike: ANCHOR + A, said quickly, is the Turkish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the seat of government of Turkey, its capital city.

clue.text: Brainbox Jethro — he's got king into it

indicators.note: with 'into it' this says the following pieces are put inside the band's name
with 'got' this says the pieces go inside the word the 'it' stands for

parts.note: Jethro Tull is a rock band, so Jethro suggests its surname-like second half, Tull
taken as written without the apostrophe
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A clever musician has managed to fit a monarch into his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brainbox' looks like a description of a clever Jethro, but it is the definition read literally: the box holding the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium is literally the box that houses the brain, a playful literal reading of a word normally meaning a clever person.

clue.text: Some intensity enshrouds 17 University

indicators.note: to enshroud is to wrap around, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: the bel is a unit for measuring intensity of sound, so it is some intensity
17-down is RUN

explanation.surface: A measure of strength surrounds a university's name.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUNEL University is in west London, named after the engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel is the name of a university in Uxbridge, west London, so it can stand for one.

clue.text: The Force knocked thrice — as would 5 and 26

parts.note: g is the symbol for the force of gravity

indicators.note: letters knocked about are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Police officers bang on the door three times, hoping to make money like two characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodney and Del Boy, the show's brothers, forever schemed to become millionaires. 'knocked' rearranges THRICE into ETRICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming wealthy was the perennial ambition of the two brothers in the sitcom, whose motto promised millionaire status by next year.

clue.text: Staff, long stuck-up one in 28 7

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: in a down clue stuck up means the word is written upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: to long for something is to have a yen for it

explanation.surface: A tall stick held aloft belongs to someone in the sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck-up' looks like snobbery but, in a down answer, turns YEN upwards into NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodney Trotter is Del Boy's younger brother, a lead character in the sitcom.

clue.text: Vigorously sick in unlicensed premises?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: BYO, bring your own, marks a restaurant without a drinks licence
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone throws up violently in a restaurant with no licence.
explanation.walkthrough: BYO means 'bring your own' (bottle), the sign of a restaurant with no alcohol licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Like billy-o is an informal British idiom meaning very hard or vigorously.

clue.text: See 28
Reliant, as 26 is on this bird?

definitions.text: Reliant, as 26 is on this bird?

parts.words: Reliant, as 26 is on this bird?
parts.note: the Reliant three-wheeler car in the sitcom is the model named after a garden bird, and Del Boy relies on robbing

explanation.surface: Someone depends on a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant was a British three-wheeled car; the Trotters drive one. 'Reliant' also hints that Del depends on taking things.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-breasted songbird which also names a famous Reliant three-wheeled car model.

clue.text: One in 28 7 is grossly stupid, and one with no right until much later

indicators.text: with no right until much later
indicators.note: the R for right is lifted out and only put back far further along

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A character is described as foolish and denied rights until late on.
explanation.walkthrough: Join CRASS, AND and A, then move the R of CRASS to the last-but-one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra is Rodney's wife in the sitcom, a character in the show.

clue.text: One in 28 7 is one lending watch chain

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against goods
an albert is a pocket-watch chain, named after Prince Albert

explanation.surface: A character in the sitcom is a pawnbroker with a timepiece chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Albert is the old sailor of the Trotter family in the sitcom, a well-known character.

clue.text: Addict for whom escort lost heart

indicators.note: losing the heart means the centre letter of the word goes

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: A drug addict whose companion has lost courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is an addict, a common informal sense of the word.

clue.text: One in 28 7, cubist left without head

indicators.note: without its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Georges Braque was a cubist painter with Picasso

explanation.surface: A sitcom character and a beheaded cubist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Raquel is Del Boy's partner in the sitcom, one of its main characters.

clue.text: Copper shot by patient chap for a sinecure

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy
Job of the Bible is proverbial for patience

explanation.surface: A policeman is shot by a patient for an easy position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman and 'patient' like someone in hospital; they are the metal and the biblical Job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is an easy, well-paid post demanding little work, which is just what the informal phrase describes.

clue.text: 17 the first steps to the most northerly mainland point?

definitions.meaning: 17-down means run, and a ... is a gentle run

definitions.text: the first steps to the most northerly mainland point
definitions.meaning: the initial letters of John o' Groats, the traditional northern tip of mainland Britain

explanation.walkthrough: John o' Groats, in Caithness, is traditionally the northern end of the British mainland; its first letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog is to run at a gentle pace, so it can stand for run, the answer to 17.

clue.text: Some pressure to exclude Rod

definitions.meaning: a rod of metal is also called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses: a unit of pressure, a verb meaning shut out, and a rigid rod.

clue.text: One in 28 7 finding Di's getting force in 4

definitions.meaning: DI replacing G (force) in GETRICH makes DIETRICH, so the forename meant is the film star's

explanation.walkthrough: Swap DI for the G of GET RICH (4) and you get DIETRICH; the answer is that actress's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene is both Boycie's wife in the sitcom and the first name of the actress Dietrich.

clue.text: Muffle the head of the rabble

definitions.meaning: to ..., in an old sense, is to wrap up the head, as in a ... cap

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an archaic verb for wrapping up the head, and a noun for a lawless crowd.

clue.text: A single series

definitions.meaning: in cricket a single scored is one ...
a ... of wins is a series of them

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a single point scored in cricket, and an unbroken sequence.

clue.text: Head of 28 7 — whose regulars serve in barges

indicators.note: taking regular letters means every other one is picked

explanation.surface: The pub's regulars serve drinks aboard river boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is the Trotters' local pub; 'regulars' looks like drinkers but picks every second letter of IN BARGES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nag's Head is the pub in the sitcom, so this word goes before Head in its name.

clue.text: Start off one in 28 7

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to set it off
The dim road sweeper in the sitcom

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning set something going, and a character in the sitcom.

clue.text: Lecher afoot, ogling skirts, getting up to overstep the mark

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
skirts means the letters lie along the edges of these words, inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A leering man on foot eyes women's skirts and gets too forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like what the lecher ogles; it marks the run RAFOOTOG, which 'getting up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To go too far is an idiom meaning to exceed acceptable limits, to overstep the mark.

clue.text: Imposing notice for one in 28 7

parts.note: grand means impressive or imposing
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A grand announcement for someone in the sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandad is the elderly relative of Del and Rodney in the early series of the sitcom.

clue.text: One getting on with book and binder

parts.note: someone getting on in years is an ager

explanation.surface: Someone getting along with a book and its binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binder' looks like part of a book but is the definition: one who wraps a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandager wraps and binds wounds, so is literally a binder of injuries.

clue.text: See 10 across
Interrupting study, is Enigmatist one in 28 7?

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of another word

parts.note: a den is a private study
the setter asks of himself: is Enigmatist, that is, am I

explanation.surface: The setter breaks into his study wondering if he is a sitcom character.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pen name; the question form makes it AM I, not I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Damien is Del Boy and Raquel's son in the sitcom.

clue.text: Happen to gamble on fish

parts.note: to bet is to gamble
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone chances a wager on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide is an old verb meaning to befall or happen to someone, as in woe betide.

clue.text: Love, very cold when climbing, beset by live one in 28 7

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on both sides by another word

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: icy means very cold

explanation.surface: A lover climbing in freezing weather is surrounded by someone in the sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Boycie is the smug car dealer in the sitcom, married to Marlene.

clue.text: Unfinished 14 breaking 500-year one in 28 7

indicators.note: breaking means one piece splits another open

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: 14-down is JOG, and to jog someone is to elbow them

explanation.surface: An incomplete run breaks a five-hundred-year record, by someone in the sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is JOG, read here as a nudge, so ELBOW, which 'Unfinished' cuts to ELBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Del Boy, Derek Trotter, is the wheeler-dealer hero of the sitcom.

clue.text: Destructive device taken over in club mob-handed

indicators.note: taken over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dangerous weapon is seized in a club by a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrogen bomb is a thermonuclear weapon of immense destructive power.

clue.text: "Hooky" Londoners also shy of working?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Dodgy Londoners keen to avoid a day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooky is British slang for stolen or dodgy goods, the Trotters' stock in trade; 'working' rearranges LONDONERS ALSO SHY OF.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom's market traders deal in dodgy, knocked-off goods, so slang for stolen fits the show.

clue.text: Out of which things don't operate sequence

definitions.text: Out of which things don't operate
definitions.meaning: a machine out of ... does not work

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: working condition, as in 'out of order', and an arrangement or sequence.

clue.text: One putting jacket on corrupt beast from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the East means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay
an animal is a beast

explanation.surface: Someone dresses a degenerate creature from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns ROT + ANIMAL into LAMINA + TOR. 'Jacket' is a plastic coating, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A laminator seals documents in a plastic coating, a protective jacket.
